question: Can a CALMem-inspired episodic strategy improve long-range conversational recall over a recent window while using less cumulative context than bounded history replay?
scope_note: Gate 1 only. This registration does not authorize runtime integration, semantic memory, cross-conversation memory, Gate 2, or Gate 3.

dataset.replay: teacher-forced fixed-prefix; candidate answers never advance the transcript or enter the index

instrument.generation_mode: streaming ProviderPort call for TTFT; one attempt; provider defaults; experiment-only string-content serializer required because the unchanged production Responses serializer returned HTTP 400 for assistant-history input
instrument.output_cap: not enforced by the current OpenAI adapter

calibration.selection_method: maximize the mean of D1 and D2 message-level Recall@k, then MRR, then delivered unique-source recall; minimize irrelevant injection, duplicate slots, query tokens, chunk size, overlap, active N, and top-k in that order
calibration.arm_order: deterministic rotation of A,B,C,D1,D2 by evaluation-step ordinal and repetition

primary_metrics.retrieval_unit: source_message_id after truncating to retrieval_top_k_chunks; no backfill
primary_metrics.echo_formula: maximum word-trigram Jaccard overlap between candidate answer and prior assistant/memory text
primary_metrics.repeated_source_amplification_formula: irrelevant unique source messages repeated from the immediately preceding evaluated query in the same conversation divided by irrelevant unique sources delivered after the first evaluated query; zero when the denominator is zero
primary_metrics.break_even_formula: earliest exchange where D cumulative logical API cost is no greater than B and remains no greater through the final exchange; null when no such exchange exists
primary_metrics.cost_basis: per-arm logical standalone cost; physical sharing disclosed separately
